objective: Add the Records tab to the Stats page (Seasons / Records / Players): Historical, with Team and Player tabs of record cards whose holder each card shows and each of which opens that record's full ranked list as a stats navigator level, and Seasonal, the per-season leaders moved off Seasons in this same unit; retire the Stats page's copy of the table CSS.
acceptance_criteria: The Stats page's route tabs are Seasons, Records and Players, in that order, as today's Tabs; /stats/records is a lazy child route (its own chunk, like SeasonsTab and PlayersTab); /stats still redirects to /stats/seasons, and the Seasons and Players addresses and teamHref and the other helpers in features/stats/links.ts keep their output for the same inputs.

Records tab: a SegmentedTabs bar Historical / Seasonal (Historical the default). The view is ?view=seasonal in the address (Historical is the default and is not written; an unknown value shows Historical), so a reload, a shared link and Back keep it. Historical holds a second SegmentedTabs bar Team / Player (Team the default, ?group=player, an unknown value shows Team) over that group's record cards, in the order GET /events/records returns them, and one line naming the data window from its since_season and through_season ("Since 2003-04, through 2026-27"; with no window, no line).

A record card shows its title as a heading (h3), "View all" at the right of the title, and its holder: the team (name) or the player (first and last name, and for a single-game record the team they played for), the value with its unit, and the season or the game's date and opponent where the record has one; a holder tied with others says so ("and 2 others" for tied_count 3); a record with no holder says nothing qualifies yet. Clicking anywhere on the card opens that record's ranked list: the card has exactly one interactive element, the "View all" link (a real address, /stats/records?record=<id>, so it can be opened in a new tab), whose accessible name includes the record's title, and whose hit area covers the whole card; the holder's name on a card is plain text (no link inside the link). Each record's rule is on its list level, not its card.

Record level: opening a card pushes a navigator level onto the Records stack, as Seasons' team level does: the breadcrumb (the navigator's "Stats path") reads "Team records › <title>" or "Player records › <title>" by the record's group, Back and the breadcrumb's first item return to Historical on that group's tab, and the address is ?record=<id> (a reload, a shared link and the browser's Back keep it; an unknown id shows the API's not-found as an in-place message with the way back). The level shows the record's title as its heading, its rule, "Since <since_season>" and its whole list (up to its top 100, total entries) in one ScrollTable: rank, the team or player (linked: a player to /players/<id>, a team to the Seasons tab filtered to it for that season through teamHref), the team a player played for, the season or the game (its date linked to /games/<id>, and the opponent), and the value. Ranks are the API's as given: a season record's rows can show the same three-place percentage with different ranks, because the API ranks the exact fraction, and the list says so in one line under the table when the record is a season record. The Historical / Seasonal bar stays above the navigator; the Team / Player bar belongs to the records level and is not shown on a record level.

Seasonal: the season's leaders, moved from Seasons in this unit (the human, 2026-10-24: never a deploy without them): a season select (?season=, the newest season by default and not written, as on Seasons) over today's Leaders section unchanged (the rule line, then the points, rebounds and assists boards); Seasons no longer renders Leaders, and nothing else on Seasons changes.

The records reads live in frontend/src/api/records.ts (fetchRecords and fetchRecord with their query keys, typed from api/schema.d.ts), with staleTime Infinity (Prompt 20 R7: the routes are cached five minutes at the edge, and the data changes once a day at most); a record's list is asked for once, at limit=100 (R11: one call shows the whole list, at most 27.5 KB); no records read passes offset.

Navigator: the record level (and the records level under it) are levels of components/stats-nav/'s StatsNavigator, so the breadcrumb, Back and the focus rule are the navigator's (focus moves to the new level's heading when a control in the navigator opens or pops a level, and not on a cold load or the browser's Back); the StatsLevel union grows; the navigator stays router-agnostic (stats-nav-lazy.test.ts's scan holds) and features/stats/ is the route adapter.

R24: the Stats page's copy of the table CSS is retired: features/stats/Stats.module.css keeps no .scroll, .table or table-cell rules, and every stats table (the leaders' included) is drawn by components/stats-nav/'s ScrollTable with the navigator's own stylesheet; ScrollTable and ColumnHeader lose their classes prop if nothing else passes it.

Accessibility: both bars are UI-010's SegmentedTabs (tablist, arrow keys, one tab stop) whose panel holds what they switch; each card is a list item in a list named by its group; "View all"'s focus ring is visible and the whole card shows the hover and focus state; every table keeps its caption, column scopes and row headers; nothing on the Records tab prints null, undefined or NaN.

Every existing frontend test passes, except where a test pins the leaders on Seasons, the two route tabs, the Seasons request counts, the Stats copy of the table CSS (stats-css.test.ts's scroll-container check for features/stats) or the only tablist on the Stats page; such a test is changed in the test commit and named in the PR body.

Baseline (provisional, the Director's, 2026-10-25; to be declared by the skeptic's first pass; before figures from origin/main 4fc9b46 as bundle-budget.test.ts's own build measures them, gzip by zlib at the default level): (a) R19: nothing but the Records route reaches the entry: no new dependency, frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/FRONTEND-019.ts declares entryJsGzipGrowth at most 150 and entryJsRawGrowth at most 400 and no entry CSS growth, and every lazy output the unit changes, adds or removes, with a gzip ceiling (R12): the Records tab's own JS at most 4.0 kB gzip and its stylesheet at most 0.8 kB, SeasonsTab, Stats.module and css:Stats.css at most their base sizes (4,637, 1,055 and 1,099; the leaders and the table CSS leave them); no chunk 500,000 bytes raw or more, and the entry under 480,000 raw (R1); the before and after build tables are in the PR body; (b) lazy: nothing in api/records.ts or the Records views is reachable from the entry by a static import, pinned by routes/lazy-routes.test.ts (RecordsTab joins its lazy pages) and stats-nav-lazy.test.ts; (c) R11, requests per screen, pinned with msw request counts through the real route table in the test kit's staleTime-0 client: a cold /stats/records makes 1 (GET /events/records); switching Team and Player makes 0; opening a card makes 1 (GET /events/records/<id>?limit=100); Back makes 0, and opening the same card again makes 0; a cold /stats/records?record=<id> makes 1, and Back from it makes 1 (the summary); a cold /stats/records?view=seasonal makes 4 (seasons, the three boards, whose rule line shares the points read), and Historical from it makes 1; a cold /stats/seasons makes 4 (before: 7; the three boards leave), and Back from a cold /stats/seasons?team=<id> makes 2 (before: 5); (d) no freeze, recorded in the PR body (Chromium Performance panel, CPU throttled 4x, 360 wide, vite preview against the branch's backend with the full load in fanwire_perf): on a cold load of /stats/records, on switching Team and Player, on opening the record with the longest list and on Back, the median long task over five alternating runs is at most 200 ms and no run over 250 ms (R4, R14), with the before figure for a cold /stats/seasons measured on origin/main and stated; (e) cumulative layout shift under 0.1 at 360 wide from a cold /stats/records to settled and on opening a record, in the worst of five runs: the cards' place holds its height while the summary loads, and the list's while the list loads; (f) every existing frontend test passes; typecheck, lint and build pass.

0x08-frontend.md gets a section of its own for this unit: the Records tab, its addresses (?view=, ?group=, ?record=, ?season=), the record levels, api/records.ts and its staleTime, the leaders' move and R24 (FrontendUI/components.md rows go in a Director PR: no unit role may write FrontendUI/).

Browser rows (vite preview against the branch's backend on its own port, reading the full load in fanwire_perf; light and dark, 360 and 1280 wide, signed out and signed in): Records opens on Historical, Team, with every team card's holder; Player shows the player cards; a click anywhere on a card, and on its View all, opens the list with the breadcrumb and Back; Back returns to the same group tab; reload keeps view, group and record; the season-record list shows its tie note; Seasonal shows the leaders for the newest season and the season select changes them; Seasons shows no leaders; the + button does not cover a card's View all at 360; keyboard only: both bars, every card's View all, the breadcrumb and Back work with a visible ring; nothing moves sideways at 360.
